entries.english:
1465 December 12. Krumau. — Johann von Rosenberg grants Hohenfurt Monastery property in the villages of Neudorf, Kropfschlag, and Reichenau.

CCL. I, Jan von Rosenberg, together with my heirs and successors, make known publicly by this letter to all who see it or hear it read that by the authority of this letter we have granted and do grant, from our own hereditary property, at Neudorf a farmstead on which Kuncz now resides and pays annually a rent of 52 groschen and 5 pennies, and an associated smallholding on which Mikl resides and pays annually 10 groschen; at Kropfschlag a farmstead on which the widow now resides and pays annually 40 groschen; and at Reichenau beneath Witkowy Kamen two homesteads with their holdings. On one resides Weniczl, who pays annually 11 groschen, 3 pennies, and 4 quarters of oats; the other was formerly occupied by Grossawar and is charged the same rent and oats as the first. From both, a tithe of rye in sheaves is to be given to our dear spiritual friends, the present and future abbot and convent of Hohenfurt Monastery. We grant this for rightful and perpetual possession and use, with full lordship and right, as we ourselves held it, reserving nothing here for ourselves. We must and promise to warrant it and free it for them against every living person, cleric or lay, who might contest it under any right, and to defend them in this as faithfully and properly as in other property granted by our forefathers. We must and promise faithfully, as soon as we are able and have the opportunity, to have the aforesaid property entered for them in the records at Prague Castle before the dean and the ecclesiastical officials there. As confirmation and to secure this more firmly, we have voluntarily given and ordered our perpetual seal to be attached to this letter. Given and written at Krumau in the year 1465 from the birth of God’s Son, on the Thursday before St. Lucy’s Day. The seal is described above.
